title: premonitions of holding a snake
content:
fear as a poison cure, past obsession, & future visioning

while traveling in South Africa for an old friend’s wedding, I went to the Lawnwood Snake Sanctuary for a guided tour (absolutely amazing, highly recommend), where I held a snake for the first time. the photo above was the first small snake I held.

I’ve always been obsessed with the visual shape and symbolism of snakes — I own multiple pieces of snake jewelry, and feel spontaneously compelled to draw them in my sketchbook (see monstera jungle snake study, and snake & moon study). perhaps it’s that snakes are one of the animals that represent the sign of Scorpio, or that I’m fascinated by their toxicity and venomous bite, or that I find their visual form aesthetically inspiring, and their skin shedding process deeply, metaphorically rich — as a physical embodiment of change and transformation.

that being said, I had never touched a snake before, and I did feel a bit scared. before giving me the first snake, our tour guide said to be careful not to drop him — it would break his back. a snake has hundreds of tiny bones in its skeletal structure. it was an important reminder to me — that even “scary” things are fragile. snakes don’t attack you without reason, our guide said — they are very calm and shy, unless you step on them. I thought about how the things we fear are also afraid of us. fear is a strange, sticky atmospheric substance. it paralyzes movement.

but then, the moment I touched the snake, all my fear evaporated. it was cool but soft, with tender skin like the flesh of a clementine. it wrapped itself around me — seeking balance, and warmth in the nook of my palm, arms, and elbows. in those first seconds, I felt as though time stretched open — and I found myself inside of it, with a soft spaciousness. in those few minutes, I had never felt so totally present in my body, and so deeply connected with the snake body, wrapping itself around me, as though I were a tree. my fear didn’t freeze me — it create an opening for total presence. my fear created a deep, profound sense of peace — a feeling that I can only describe as deep, spiritual pleasure.


the moment I touched the snake, I had a premonition — that this coming year, as I enter my annual tradition of a hard, transformative Scorpio season — I would do many things that scare me, as I’ve done before — and this time, I would be more ready for them. my fear would transform into peace, and pleasure — almost instantly, upon touch, like a poison cure.

the next immediate thing on my itinerary was: bungee jumping from a bridge. I wasn’t planning on doing it (I’m afraid of heights), but I knew, after watching how my fear alchemized itself, that I absolutely had to.
